subject: Helios.ai — Implementation Runway: VPC Peering & On-Prem Package Checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@helios.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Helios.ai private deployment kickoff — initial info & checklist

Evelyn — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a short 'implementation runway' that outlines the networking and on-prem package decisions we'll need to finalize before we hand off to infra for install. Key asks for your team to supply before the technical review: 

- Primary network contact (name + best contact) for peering and TGW decisions
- AWS account numbers for peering and for any PrivateLink endpoints
- VPC CIDR(s) you plan to use for the Redwood runtime (we recommend a /16 or /20 depending on scale)
- Whether you prefer Transit Gateway (TGW) peering or VPC peering for communication between Redwood-hosted control plane and private deployment
- If on-prem appliance will be used: public IPs, firewall egress rules, and serial number if already provisioned
- Compliance requirement: where should KMS be hosted (Helios-managed KMS in your account, or Redwood-managed CMK)?

Proposed next step: 60-minute network review (detailed CIDR mapping + security controls) sometime this week. I've attached implementation-runway-v0.1.pdf which has a draft checklist and timeline. 

Thanks — looking to lock the network review by Friday.

— Jordan
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: implementation-runway-v0.1.pdf (6 pages)

From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@helios.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Lee <dan.lee@helios.ai>, Helios.ai Security <security@helios.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2028 18:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Helios.ai private deployment kickoff — initial info & checklist

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and attachments below. Dan Lee (cc'd) will be our network lead and available for the detailed review. Our security lead (security@helios.ai) is available for any KMS or key handling questions.

Provided info: 
- Network lead: Dan Lee, dan.lee@helios.ai, +1 415-555-0123
- AWS accounts: Production: 987654321012, Staging (air-gapped): 987654321013
- VPCs: prod VPC 10.10.0.0/16, staging VPC 10.20.0.0/16
- Preference: We prefer PrivateLink for control-plane traffic and TGW for data VPC-to-VPC connectivity. We use AWS Transit Gateway managed by our infra team (no third-party transit).
- On-prem: We will run the Redwood on-prem appliance in staging (air-gapped). We'll need an offline installer and signed package. Firewall will only allow outbound TLS to specific IPs; we'll provide egress allowlist.
- KMS: Compliance requires customer-managed CMK in our prod account for any customer key material.

Attached: helios-network-inventory.xlsx (CIDR mapping + BGP neighbor info).

We can do the network review Thu 26 Jan 2028 11:00 PT if that works for your team.

— Evelyn
Head of IT Ops, Helios.ai

Attachments: helios-network-inventory.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jan 2028 19:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Helios.ai network info & proposed implementation split

Team — forwarding Helios' reply (see attachment). Summary and proposal: 

Summary: Helios prefers PrivateLink for control plane, TGW for data plane. Prod/staging accounts and CIDRs attached (10.10.0.0/16 prod, 10.20.0.0/16 staging). Staging will be air-gapped — they require an offline installer and signed on-prem package. KMS must be customer-managed CMK in prod account.

Proposal (action items):
- Monica: lead the TGW/VPC peering verification and verify our PrivateLink endpoint requirements vs. their TGW config.
- Ben: validate the egress allowlist and make sure our runtime endpoints and IP ranges are covered; produce a definitive list we can ship to Helios.
- Dev: prepare an offline installer flow and signed package instructions for their staging air-gapped environment; include checksum verification and step-by-step install.
- Irene: produce a minimal S3/Artifact hosting plan for signed packages (s3 presigned URL pattern), plus process for secure transfer to Helios staging.

Can we get owners to ack and estimate ETA? I booked a 60-minute network review Thu 26 Jan 11:00 PT (Meet link below) — please plan to join. I'm including Dan Lee and Evelyn on the external invite.

Meet: https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij
Doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-Helios/Implementation-Runway
JIRA: INFRA-1348 (Helios: networking review)

— Jordan

Attachments: sow_helios_v1.docx (SOW draft)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jan 2028 08:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Helios.ai network info & proposed implementation split

Ack — I can own the TGW verification. Notes from my side: 

- We need to confirm whether Helios' TGW enforces route table propagation per-account or per-attachment; that will change how we propose route targets.
- Firewall/IPS requirements: we'll request an explicit list of outbound IPs + FQDNs from Ben; if they restrict via IP only we should provide both CIDR and exact IP ranges.
- For the on-prem offline package: we should add a step to rotate credentials post-install and provide an automated key enrollment script so their security team can attest to key handover.

Dev — please draft the offline installer README with a SHA256 checksum step and a signed manifest. I'll review before we send to Helios.

I can be on the network review Thu 26 Jan 11:00 PT.

— Monica
Senior Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference
